Subject: Post-demo model shortlist & next steps

Alex / Bethany — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the model shortlist we recommend for your use case (customer support summarization + intent classification) based on the prompts you shared and the latency/cost targets you gave (~100ms median, <$0.0008/token target):

Summary of recommended shortlist (tradeoffs):
- Redwood-3B-quant (recommended first cut)
  - Cost: lowest of the three (quantized path)
  - Latency: ~40–170ms median on Dedicated T4-like profile
  - Quality: good for summarization, may miss edge-case nuance on long threads
  - Risk: some regression risk on hallucination-sensitive prompts; suggest prompt-tuning/eval set

- Llama-2-13B-q4
  - Cost: mid-range
  - Latency: ~70–120ms depending on batching
  - Quality: better handling of multi-turn context and instruction-following; strong balance
  - Risk: stable, widely used baseline; less aggressive quantization than 3B path

- OpenLlama-33B (float32 / mixed precision)
  - Cost: highest (larger footprint)
  - Latency: ~180–300ms unless we use batching/long-tail routing to faster nodes
  - Quality: best for edge-case accuracy and more complex summarization tasks
  - Risk: higher cost and longer inference times; good as a fallback for low-frequency high-importance requests

Attachments and assets included: attached model-benchmarks.pdf (aggregate bench, cost/latency by seq len) and prompt-sets.csv (the evaluation prompts you gave, plus our extended edge-case set). Also linked: https://redwood.inference/benchmarks/ACME-2026-089 for the live benchmark dashboard.

Recommended next steps (proposed):
1) Agree on shortlist to run a 72-hour eval (we recommend Redwood-3B-quant + Llama-2-13B-q4 as the initial pair).
2) We run the eval in an isolated Dedicated pool (same routing/pinning you would use in production) using your prompt set + our edge-case prompts (~5k prompts total).
3) Deliver per-prompt quality metrics (accuracy, extractive F1 where applicable), latency distribution, and a regression alert summary if any prompts degrade vs your baseline.
4) Follow-up call to review results and choose the production model + rollout policy (canary -> staged rollout).

Can we schedule the kick-off eval for next week? I have availability Wed/Thu 11am–3pm ET. If that works I'll send a follow-up with test plan and access instructions.

Perfect — Wed 11am ET works, I'll send a calendar invite shortly. Quick answers inline to your questions: 

- PII controls / eval environment: yes, we can run the eval in a Dedicated private pool with customer-managed KMS and VPC isolation. That environment will not stream logs to the hosted plane; we can enable audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket or ship them to your SIEM. I've CC'd Stephanie (our security solutions lead) to add any SOC2 / data-flow docs you need.

- Cost delta for staged rollout: typically a staged rollout (5–10% canary for 48hrs) adds ~6–12% incremental compute cost during the canary window (depends on traffic distribution) because you run the canary in parallel while the rest of traffic routes to the baseline. If we move from canary -> 100% and the new model is more expensive per-token, the clear one-time delta is proportional to token volume. We'll include a cost projection in the eval report.

Next items I'll attach to the kickoff invite:
- Short test plan (what we run during the 72-hour eval)
- Access instructions for Dedicated pool (IAM/KMS checklist)
- Baseline metric templates we'll deliver (latency histograms, per-prompt quality table, regression alerts)

If either of you want a deeper look at our prompt-level regression detection logic before Wed, I can share a short explainer doc — otherwise we'll review it on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.
